title: Orbital garden
description: A living sculpture of light and metal. Shape its bloom, find a palette, and explore the ribbons of a small procedural universe.
try_it: Drag to orbit. Open and close the bloom, switch to Ember, or pause the motion. Click a ribbon to select it; the focused canvas also accepts arrow keys.
explanation: Rust signals own the shape, palette, pause control, and selection. A normal JavaScript module subscribes to them and renders with Three.js. Raycasting sends a CustomEvent back to Rust. Resetting or leaving disposes the frame loop, observer, and GPU resources.

title: Your week, in motion
description: An interactive chart with ordinary Chart.js code and real Rust state. Change the data, pick a day, and watch both sides respond.
try_it: Select a point in the chart, then add 12 visits to that day. Load the next week or switch off smoothing. Day buttons provide the same selection by keyboard.
explanation: The dataset, curve setting, and selected day are Rust signals exposed with JsInputs. The JavaScript module creates one Chart.js instance and subscribes to those inputs. Chart clicks dispatch a native event whose numeric detail is checked in Rust. Resetting or leaving destroys the chart.
preview_detail: Change a signal. Move the line.

title: One picture, several threads
description: Paint a fractal with a pool of up to 16 compute threads, and see which thread painted each tile.
try_it: Press Race to compare painting one tile at a time with painting tiles across the pool. Click anywhere on the picture to zoom in and cancel the previous view. Turn on the thread colors to see who painted what.
explanation: The pool provides up to 16 compute threads, bounded by the browser’s hardware hint. One streaming task hands tiles to the compute threads and sends each finished tile back as it is ready. Zooming cancels the previous stream. Without shared memory the same picture is painted by one ordinary worker.

title: Four in a row
description: Play against an engine that thinks on another thread. Watch it weigh every column while the board stays yours.
try_it: Drop a disc. While the engine thinks, the bars above the board show how it rates each column, sharpening as it looks further ahead. Press Move now to make it decide early, or choose Deep and try to beat it.
explanation: The engine is a stateful worker that remembers positions between moves. Each move is one call that reports progress after every column it weighs. Move now cancels that call, and the page plays the best move reported so far. The rules are one Rust module shared by the page and the worker.

title: A million books in a worker
description: Search a million generated books kept inside a worker. Each query sends only the search text and filter.
try_it: Type a word such as “moon” or a name such as “ada”, and watch the counts change. Pick a genre to filter. Type quickly: older replies cannot replace your latest results.
explanation: The worker builds the million books once, when the demo starts, and keeps them. Each keystroke calls one method on its typed client with a tiny query. A Resource cancels the previous call when the query changes, so a stale answer never replaces a newer one.
preview_detail: search a dataset kept in a worker

title: Async and coherent async
description: The same data, updated separately or together.
try_it: Wait for Notebook to load, then choose Sketchbook.
explanation: Async shows each result as it arrives. Coherent async keeps the previous complete result until both are ready.

title: A reactive workspace
description: Name a workspace, change the seat count, and watch a cached total update with the HTML.
try_it: Rename the workspace, add a few seats, then switch to annual billing. The total follows both signals.
explanation: The inputs write to signals. A memo reads the seat count and billing choice to calculate the total. HTML bindings read those values directly; there is no render function to call.

title: Rows with a memory
description: Reorder a reading list while each row keeps its own editable note and identity.
try_it: Write a note on the first row, then reverse the list. The note moves with that book. Remove a row or add another to see the list reconcile.
explanation: ForEach repeats the inline li for each book. The stable id keeps that row's identity; item and index are reactive handles supplied by the list. Reordering moves the same DOM and preserves the native note input. Removing a book disposes its row.

title: Work with a lifetime
description: Mount a ticking panel, remove it, and see its timer stop when its owner is disposed.
try_it: Wait for a few ticks, then remove the panel. The count stops. Mount it again to start a new timer, with an event log showing each lifecycle transition.
explanation: The child starts an interval in on_activate. Its on_cleanup callback drops the timer and records disposal. The parent owns the visible tick count, so you can observe that no work continues after the child is gone.

title: An async field guide
description: Fetch local field notes with loading, retained results, cancellation, and a recoverable error.
try_it: Choose a destination, or change your choice before it finishes. Try the simulated error, then retry. The previous note remains labeled with the destination it actually belongs to.
explanation: A Resource tracks the selected key and fetches a text fixture served by this docs app. A deliberate 700 ms delay makes loading visible. The error button simulates a one-time loader failure; retry runs the same key again. Changing the key cancels obsolete work.

title: One complete product view
description: Load price and stock at different speeds while publishing one consistent product view.
try_it: Switch products after the first one loads. Price takes 300 ms; stock takes 1,100 ms. The old complete product stays visible until the new name, price, and stock can appear together.
explanation: Two child components declare independent AsyncValue reads. The Async component stages their updates and publishes the region only when both are ready. Selection controls and loading status live outside the boundary. Values come from local HTTP fixtures with artificial delays.

title: Shared, without passing props
description: Change a workspace accent and let nested components read it from their nearest owner.
try_it: Pick Forest or Violet. The nested preview reads the same signal from context. This changes the demo's accent, independently of the documentation's color theme.
explanation: The parent provides a signal under the Accent context key. A nested child retrieves that exact type from its owner without an accent argument. Context lookup supplies the handle; reading the signal makes the HTML reactive.
preview_detail: A typed value, shared by descendants
